summary: Same Halloween orange/purple band palette and band spacing, but the port's bands are essentially straight and frozen — its wave amplitude is ~10x too small (invisible at the default 16x16 rig) and it has zero horizontal drift, against an original whose bands snake by a full band-width and continuously translate and reshape.
observations: Both sides render cleanly on the default grid rig (16x16, 256 px): no compile or runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both, no controls on either side (probe: '(no settable controls)' for orig and port).

Global levels match well: over 240 s at 2 fps meanBrightness avg 54.8 (orig) vs 56.0 (port), both brightnessTrend 'steady', zeroMotionFrames 1/480 on both. Channel means orig R93/G29/B43 vs port R94/G34/B40 — the port is a touch more yellow-orange and slightly less blue-purple, a minor palette-weight difference only.

Palette family matches: measured hues on the default rig are orange 7-29 deg and purple 252-288 deg on the original, orange 7-36 deg and purple 270-288 deg on the port. Same two-family Halloween scheme.

Band count and spacing match. Classifying pixels orange-vs-purple, a row of 48 px carries 3 purple bands (~16 px pitch) on BOTH sides at t=0 (orig row0 purple runs at x=0, 5-9, 24-27, 44-47; port at x=11-14, 29-32, 43-47). Same 3 bands per grid width on the default 16x16 rig.

MOTION is the headline divergence. motion stat at 20 fps: orig 12.6 avg vs port 1.0 avg (baseline); at 5 fps over 60 s, orig 39 vs port 3; at 2 fps over 240 s, orig 52 vs port 7.9. motionLit tracks motion exactly on both (dense pattern), so this is not a sparseness artefact. In the baseline filmstrip (orig-motion.png / port-motion.png, 3.00-3.55 s) consecutive original frames visibly redraw while consecutive port frames are near-identical.

The port has NO horizontal band travel at all. Circular cross-correlation of the orange/purple column field against t=0 gives orig +1 px at t=1 s, +3 px at t=2 s, -9 px at t=3 s (48x48 grid), while the port gives exactly 0, 0, 0 at every one of those times.

The port's waviness is ~10x too shallow. Measuring the per-row spatial-DFT phase of the k=3 band component and converting to pixels: on the 48x48 grid the original's band edge wanders 14.7-15.8 px peak-to-peak across the 48 rows (i.e. about one full band pitch) at every sampled time from t=0 to t=55 s; the port's wanders 1.3-1.7 px. On the pattern's DEFAULT 16x16 rig the same measurement gives orig 4.0-4.9 px pk-pk (again ~one band pitch) vs port 0.48-0.62 px — sub-pixel, so on the default rig the port's hue is literally constant down each column (hue standard deviation down a column measures 0 for most columns at t=0, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 39 s) and it reads as straight vertical stripes.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way (3 bands and ~one-band-pitch-proportional wave at both 16x16 and 48x48), so the amplitude gap is a coefficient difference, not a rig-mapping difference.

The port's spatial structure is rigid over time; the original's is not. Normalised spatial-power at k=1..8 on the 48x48 grid is essentially constant on the port across t=0..55 s (k3 power 0.221-0.226, k4 0.094-0.113 every sample), while the original's dominant wavenumber shuffles between k=1, 2, 3 and 5 with power moving between them — the original's bands widen, narrow, merge and split as they travel; the port's never change.
The port's k=3 power (0.225) is far more concentrated than the original's (0.03-0.10 spread over k=1..7): the port's stripes are cleaner and more regular, the original's are more irregular/organic.

One thing the port does get right in motion: the ripple propagates VERTICALLY at a comparable rate on both sides. Cross-correlating the per-row band-phase profile against t=0 gives orig -8 rows at t=1 s and -20/-21 rows at t=2 s, port 0 rows at t=1 s and -14 rows at t=2 s. The mechanism is there, just applied at ~1/10 amplitude.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): the horizontal-drift and vertical-ripple displacements above are identical at --fps 10, 20 and 40 for each side. Frame-rate coupling is NOT a factor here.
Not RNG-driven: seed 1234 reproduces the baseline stats exactly on both sides (orig mean 55 motion 13, port mean 56 motion 1).

Steady state matches the opening: the survey (60 s at 5 fps) and extended survey (240 s at 2 fps) rhythm images show one uniform regime on each side with no mode boundaries, and a late window parked at t=220-232 s (48x48) is indistinguishable in character from t=0 on both sides — original still snaking hard, port still a stationary gentle ripple. Neither side dies, decays or saturates.
Net viewer impression: the original is a field of orange/purple stripes writhing like flames or oil-on-water; the port is orange/purple striped wallpaper with a faint standing shimmer.
feedback: The port's band-displacement (wave) amplitude is roughly 10x too small. Measured on the default 16x16 rig the original's bands snake 4.0-4.9 px peak-to-peak across the 16 rows — about one full band pitch — while the port's snake 0.5-0.6 px, i.e. sub-pixel, which is why the port renders as perfectly straight vertical stripes at the default resolution. Multiply the per-row horizontal offset by about 8-10x. Confirm the fix on the default 16x16 rig, not just at 48x48: at the default rig the hue should visibly differ down a single column, which today it does not at all.

The port is missing the original's horizontal band DRIFT entirely. The original's whole band field translates sideways (measured against t=0 on a 48x48 grid: +1 px at 1 s, +3 px at 2 s, -9 px at 3 s — a wandering, non-monotonic drift, not a steady scroll), while the port measures exactly 0 px at every time and every frame rate. Add the time-varying horizontal offset to the band coordinate; without it the pattern reads as a static wallpaper.

The port's band structure is too rigid. The original's dominant spatial wavenumber moves between 1, 2, 3 and 5 over a 60 s window and its energy is spread across k=1..7, so bands visibly widen, narrow, merge and split as they travel. The port's spectrum is frozen (k=3 power 0.221-0.226, k=4 0.094-0.113 at every sample from t=0 to t=55 s) and over-concentrated on k=3, giving stripes that are cleaner and more mechanically regular than the original's. Whatever term modulates band pitch over time on the original is missing or has near-zero amplitude on the port.

Overall animation energy needs to come up ~10x to match: motion 12.6 (orig) vs 1.0 (port) at 20 fps, 39 vs 3 at 5 fps, 52 vs 7.9 at 2 fps. Use that ratio as the acceptance check after the amplitude and drift fixes land.

Do NOT touch these — they already match: overall brightness (55 vs 56 mean), the orange/purple hue families, the band count (3 purple bands across the grid width on both), the band pitch (~16 px on a 48-wide grid), the vertical ripple propagation rate (comparable on both sides), fps-invariance (both time-based), and steady-state stability (both steady out to 240 s).

Minor colour nitpick, worth a look only after the motion work: the port's mean green is 33.6 vs the original's 28.7 and its mean blue 39.9 vs 42.8, so the port's oranges sit slightly more yellow and its purples slightly less blue. Its purple hues cluster at 270-288 deg where the original's run 252-288 deg.
